The Struggle To Commoditize AI

Tilly Zhang

Gavekal Dragonomics | 21 Oct 2026

The jitters in global equity markets suggest that investors are getting more worried about how the leading US artificial-intelligence model developers are going to make money: the shares of AI-related hardware and software firms sold off last week after Anthropic’s latest quarterly revenue growth disappointed some market participants. But those same worries about monetization surfaced much earlier—and in a more dramatic way—in China, where the leading AI companies have seen their share prices decline substantially in recent months.The investor concern is understandable: while China’s open-weight models have surged in popularity, the companies are struggling to translate that usage into revenue growth. The problem is that China’s AI developers are pursuing a low-margin, high-volume business of offering cheap models to a vast number of users, in part because they expect the entire industry to eventually become commoditized. But US export controls on advanced chips mean that they cannot scale up computing power enough to meet rising demand. Those limitations might ease over time as domestic chip production expands, but for now the capacity constraints are materially limiting the revenue growth of China’s AI developers.
